newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to revise law for forex deregulation - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to revise law for forex deregulation - MOF.

text.p: A key Japanese government panel has started discussing the details of a planned revision of foreign exchange laws to allow an expansion of currency transactions by corporations, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Thursday.

The committee, which is an advisory panel to the finance minister, will aim to come up with a report on the details by the end of the year, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, told a news conference.

Sakakibara said the Finance Minister asked the committee to come up with the details of the revision, and added that a subcommittee would start specific discussions at its first meeting on September 25.
The revision will be to implement the deregulation measures which the committee called for in June.

It said at the time that the amendments would establish the qualifications for new participants allowed to carry out currency transactions, the range of businesses they can cover, and the extent of the finance ministry's supervision.
Financial sources said the businesses that new participants would be allowed to engage in would include currency transactions, loans to overseas companies, and derivatives.
Regular banking business such as foreign currency deposits and overseas remittances would be excluded, the sources said.
The revision is widely expected to be submitted to the next ordinary parliament session early next year, but Sakakibara only said that MOF would aim to do so as soon as possible.
The subcommittee will also discuss how to invigorate the Tokyo offshore financial market, Sakakibara said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3710)
